text.title: North Star Metric Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when choosing and operating a North Star Metric. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix and maps to a rule in 01-core-rules.xml.

antipattern.symptom: The decision record adopts "MRR", "new signups" or "monthly active users" as the NSM; product cannot name a feature that moves it this quarter, and marketing already owns the number.

root-cause.source: Sean Ellis and Morgan Brown, Hacking Growth (2017)

antipattern.root-cause: The team picked the number the board already asks for instead of the moment the customer receives value; lagging outcome mistaken for leading indicator.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-nsm-counts-value-delivered: restate candidates as counts of the core value event, keep revenue as the outcome the NSM is validated against, and rescore under r-candidates-scored-against-criteria.

antipattern.symptom: Two dashboards show different NSM values for the same week; the analytics team and the growth team disagree on whether trial accounts and internal workspaces count.
antipattern.root-cause: The definition names a concept ("active teams") but not the event, threshold, window and exclusions; each consumer filled the gaps differently.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-nsm-definition-computable: write the event list, unit, window and inclusion rules into the definition slot, publish one dashboard URL, and have a second analyst reproduce the number before adoption.

antipattern.symptom: The record states the NSM "is a leading indicator of retention" with no cohort numbers; a year later the NSM is up 40 percent and 90-day retention is unchanged.

root-cause.source: Amplitude, The North Star Playbook (2019); Hacking Growth (2017)

antipattern.root-cause: The leading-indicator claim was borrowed from a case study (Slack, Facebook) rather than tested on the product's own cohorts.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-nsm-validated-against-retention: run the above-threshold vs below-threshold cohort comparison, record cohort size, period and delta in the validation section, and do not adopt on "inconclusive".

antipattern.symptom: The record names a "primary NSM" for product and a "secondary NSM" for marketing; quarterly planning stalls when the two point in different directions.

root-cause.source: Sean Ellis, North Star Metric concept

antipattern.root-cause: The team avoided the trade-off the NSM exists to settle by giving each function its own star.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-single-nsm: keep one NSM, move the runner-up into the input tree under r-input-metrics-tree or record it as a rejected candidate with its reason.

antipattern.symptom: Every team's OKR reads "grow the NSM by 20 percent"; nobody can say which of their initiatives touches it; the number moves and nobody knows why.

root-cause.source: Amplitude, The North Star Playbook (2019), inputs framework

antipattern.root-cause: The NSM was adopted as a slogan without decomposition into owned, movable inputs.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-input-metrics-tree: define three to five inputs (breadth, depth, frequency, efficiency), assign each to a team with current value and target, and rewrite OKRs against the inputs.

antipattern.symptom: The NSM chart rises steadily after a notification campaign or a bot integration launch; paired retention and revenue are flat; the threshold in the definition was quietly lowered last quarter.
antipattern.root-cause: The record never named how the metric could be inflated, so the first team under pressure found the cheapest way to move it.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-nsm-resists-gaming and r-nsm-change-is-a-new-record: add exclusions and a paired quality metric to the definition, and treat any threshold or definition change as a new linked decision record with a series-break date.

section.title: Human checkpoint
section.p: Before any binding action driven by a North Star Metric output (publish, send, rollout, commit), a named human reviewer must sign off. The agent surfaces a `ready_for_review=true` flag and does NOT auto-commit decisions, copy, configs, or rollouts.
